status_summary: On 2025-03-21 EOIR reinstated its 2019 policy on status dockets (PM 25-27), and on 2025-04-18 its Acting Director issued PM 25-29, rescinding the 2021 memo on administrative closure and stating that no statute authorizes it, while noting the 2024 rule stayed binding until rescinded or vacated. On 2026-06-22 the Northern District of Texas entered a consent judgment in Texas v. DOJ declaring the 2024 EOIR docket rule contrary to law and vacating it, and, per an advocacy advisory, barring DOJ from rules allowing administrative closure without a statutory basis; on 2026-08-21 the court denied a motion by cities and a legal services group to intervene, and they appealed to the Fifth Circuit. The actions limit immigration judges' closure authority; ICE's own use of termination and closure motions was not shown to have changed by a written policy.

timeline.event: EOIR Acting Director issued PM 25-29, effective the same day, cancelling Director's Memorandum 22-03 (2021) on administrative closure, stating that no statute authorizes administrative closure by EOIR adjudicators and that EOIR would not defend the 2024 docket management rule against legal challenge, while noting the rule remained binding until rescinded, superseded, enjoined, vacated or found unlawful.

In Texas v. DOJ (N.D. Tex., No. 7:26-cv-00070) Chief Judge Reed O'Connor granted a joint motion and entered an Order and Final Judgment (ECF 5) the same day the complaint was filed, declaring the 2024 EOIR docket management rule (89 FR 46742) in excess of statutory authority and contrary to law; per an advocacy advisory the judgment also vacated the rule and enjoined DOJ from rules allowing administrative closure without an express statutory basis, and the parties waived appeal.
The district court denied a motion by Baltimore, Columbus, New Haven and Centro Legal de la Raza to intervene and defend the 2024 rule; the movants appealed to the Fifth Circuit.

title: End administrative closure and termination of pending immigration cases
uncertainties: The Mandate's pages 141 and 152 address ICE's use of closure and termination, while the actions found are by EOIR and a court, which control the immigration judge's authority; the record is therefore a partial match. The consent judgment's docket text (ECF 3 and ECF 5, signed by Chief Judge O'Connor) was read on a case-tracking page, which reports a declaration that the 2024 rule is in excess of statutory authority and contrary to law; the order itself was not opened because the court's docket host refused access, and the vacatur and the bar on future closure rules come from a September 2026 advocacy advisory (no day given) and a news report. The intervention denial and the Fifth Circuit appeal come from the advisory only; the case-tracking docket (last updated 2026-07-26) does not show them. The 2026 BIA interim final rule does not change closure rules per the portion read; a Federal Register search of EOIR rules since 2025-01-20 found no rule on administrative closure or termination. PM 25-27 is cited from the advisory only. The EOIR policy memorandum list page failed to load, so other memos since 2025-01-20 may exist. Whether the Attorney General acted was not found. The vacatur follows a suit by Texas that DOJ did not defend. Independent review of 2026-10-16: PM 25-29, the case-tracking docket and the September 2026 advisory were re-read and agree with the record; the docket page shows the case closed on 2026-06-22 with no intervention or appeal entries, so the 2026-08-21 denial and the Fifth Circuit appeal rest on the advisory alone.
